cards.explanation: The answer is commended. Paul says, “…you should have commended me…” He says they drove him to being a fool, so a little credit was in order. I'd want a pat on the hat myself in that spot, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says he is “…in no way inferior…” to those super-apostles, which is a bold thing to say. Then in that same sentence he adds, “even though I am nothing.” A big claim and a humble one, all in one breath, friends.

The answer is signs, wonders, and miracles. Paul says “…signs, wonders, and miracles…” were performed among the Corinthians. He adds that they were done with great perseverance. The Corinthians were right there among it, bakers.

The answer is True. Paul asks, “In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you?” So the one difference he names is that he didn't burden them. Then he adds, “Forgive me this wrong!” I think that line has a twinkle in it.

The answer is that he wants them and not their things. Paul says, “…I am not seeking your possessions, but you.” He's not coming to collect. He's coming for the people, and I'd take that guest over the one who eyes my cookie jar, friends.

The answer is parents for their children. Paul says, “For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.” The saving goes from parents to children. Just before that he says he is “…not seeking your possessions, but you.”

The answer is himself. Paul says, “…I will most gladly spend my money and myself.” He's not only opening his wallet, he's giving his whole self. That's a big gift, friends, and he says he gives it most gladly.
The answer is False. Paul says, “…I will most gladly spend my money and myself.” That's the opposite of grudging, and it's for the sake of the Corinthians' souls. He's happy to pour it out, bakers.

The answer is Titus. Paul urged Titus to go visit the Corinthians and sent another brother along too. Elsewhere he calls Titus his partner and fellow worker (2 Corinthians 8:23). Then Paul asks, “Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?”
The answer is False. The verse says, “I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him.” So Titus had company, friends. Paul doesn't name the brother, so I won't either.

The answer is that Titus acted just as Paul did. Paul asks, “Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?” Same Spirit, same footsteps. That's his point about himself and Titus, friends.

The answer is build up. Paul says, “We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.” He's not on trial, friends. He's building. And he calls them beloved while he does it.

The answer is True. Paul says, “…I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish.” So the worry runs both ways, bakers. I think he knows the visit could be a bumpy one.

The answer is quarreling, jealousy, and gossip. Paul says, “I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.” That's a list of eight, and those three are on it. He fears they may be there when he comes, friends, and every one of them is about how people treat each other.

The answer is humble. Paul says, “I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you…” It's a fear, friends, not a sure thing. He adds that he will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier.

The answer is repented. Paul says he'll be grieved over many who “…have sinned earlier and have not repented…” To repent means to turn from it, and he's grieved because they haven't. I think that comes from a heart that loves them, bakers.
